name: Property For Industry Limited
overview: Property For Industry Limited (PFI) is a New Zealand-listed, internally-managed pure-play industrial property REIT, owning a portfolio of more than 90 industrial properties valued at over NZ$2.25 billion, concentrated (~85-88%) in Auckland. Listed on the NZX since 1994 and internally managed since 30 June 2017, PFI generates income by leasing warehouse, logistics and light-industrial buildings to a diversified base of 120+ tenants, supplementing rental growth with a multi-year development and redevelopment pipeline. It targets 75-90% core generic industrial holdings, with the balance in development opportunities and specialised assets, and has moved its fiscal year end from 31 December to 30 June (effective FY2024/25).

business_model.summary: PFI earns essentially all of its income from rental and management fee income on a portfolio of leased industrial buildings, supplemented by fair-value gains/losses on investment property (non-cash) and periodic development margin capture. FY2025 rental and management fee income was NZ$127.5m (net rental income NZ$108.0m); H1 FY2026 rental and management fee income was NZ$73.6m, up 20.2% year-on-year, driven by rent reviews, new leasing and newly completed developments (30-32 Bowden Road, 78 Springs Road Stage 1). The company distributes the large majority of its Adjusted Funds From Operations (AFFO) as dividends, with FY2026 cash dividends of 9.50 cps (up 10.5% on FY2025) and FY2027 dividend guidance of 9.75-9.85 cps.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - industrial, logistics, warehousing and light-manufacturing tenants (SME to large corporate, e.g. Daikin, Fisher & Paykel, GrainCorp, MiTek)
business_model.geographic_mix: Auckland ~85-88% of portfolio by value; balance in other North Island/South Island centres (e.g. Hamilton, Mt Maunganui, Christchurch)

competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest pure-play industrial landlords on the NZX; Goodman Property Trust is larger by market cap (~NZ$2.9bn) and also industrial-focused, while Argosy and other REITs are diversified across office/retail/industrial. PFI differentiates as a 100% industrial specialist concentrated in supply-constrained Auckland industrial land.

moat_factors.description: Limited zoned industrial land in Auckland's core precincts (East Tamaki, Penrose, Mt Wellington, Avondale, Manukau) constrains new supply and supports occupancy (99.9% at Dec-2025, 98.7% at Jun-2026) and rental growth
Management internalised in 2017, removing external management fees and aligning management/shareholder interests; one of the lowest management expense ratios among listed NZ property vehicles
120-125+ tenants across 90+ properties and multiple industrial sub-sectors reduces single-tenant/single-site concentration risk
Track record of >55,000 sqm of 5 Green Star industrial space delivered since 2024 on time/budget; captures development margin (~15-20%) unavailable to passive landlords
Portfolio persistently under-rented versus market (~11.5% at Jun-2025, ~9.1% at Dec-2025, ~7.1% at Jun-2026), providing a multi-year organic rental growth runway as reviews and renewals occur

weaknesses: Geographic concentration risk: ~85-88% of the portfolio is in Auckland, exposing PFI to a single regional economy/property cycle
Small-cap scale relative to Goodman Property Trust limits capital markets flexibility and cost of capital advantage
Development pipeline execution risk (leasing risk on speculative components, e.g. Springs Road Stage 2)
High payout ratio (FY2026 dividend ~95% of AFFO on a one-year basis) leaves limited retained capital buffer, increasing reliance on debt/equity markets to fund growth

growth_drivers: Rent reversion: closing the gap between passing/contract rent and market rent (~7-11% under-rented across recent periods) as leases roll to review or renewal

Development and redevelopment pipeline: ~$325-350m of committed/potential capital investment across 11 planned Green Star projects (Springs Road, Harris Road, Spedding Road, Neilson Street, Patiki Road, Rosebank Road, Nesdale Avenue, Cryers Road) to be progressively delivered over 3-5 years
Falling New Zealand interest rates/OCR cuts reducing weighted average cost of debt (down from 5.72% in Jun-2024 to 4.52% in Jun-2025 and 4.54% at Dec-2025) and supporting cap rates/valuations
Selective bolt-on acquisitions in core Auckland industrial precincts (e.g. 505-507 Mt Wellington Highway, 11C Norris Avenue, Hamilton) funded by recycling non-core/out-of-Auckland divestments
Sustainability-linked demand: growing occupier preference for Green Star-rated, energy-efficient industrial space supports premium rents and tenant retention
Long WALT (5.0-5.5 years) and low near-term expiry exposure (just ~1.2% of contract rent expiring in FY2026) providing income visibility while reversion plays out

business.description: ~85-88% of portfolio value is in a single city/region; a local economic downturn, oversupply of industrial land, or infrastructure disruption disproportionately affects PFI versus more geographically diversified peers

Speculative components of the development pipeline (e.g. part of Springs Road Stage 2, ~$325-350m of committed/potential capital) carry leasing, cost-overrun and delivery timing risk before they generate contracted income
Reliance on manufacturing, logistics and distribution tenants exposes PFI to NZ economic cycles, freight volumes and consumer demand

financial.description: Total borrowings of ~NZ$768-770m as at Dec-2025, ~80% hedged; as older, lower-rate swaps roll off and are replaced at prevailing rates, interest costs can rise even in a falling-OCR environment; weighted average cost of debt was 4.54% at Dec-2025

Gearing of 34.2% at Dec-2025/Jun-2026 (covenant <50%, target range ~30-40%) is expected to rise toward the mid-point of the target range (~35.7%) as committed acquisitions and development capex are drawn; a sharp valuation decline would compress covenant headroom (LVR covenant, ICR >2.0x covenant)

FY2026 dividend guidance implies a one-year AFFO payout ratio of ~95% (FY2027 guidance similarly elevated), leaving little retained cash buffer and increasing reliance on debt/equity markets to fund the development pipeline

Reliance on bank facilities, NZDX bonds (PFI020 repaid Oct-2025, PFI030 $150m, PFI040 $200m issued Apr-2026) and the Pricoa US private placement; a deterioration in credit markets could raise funding costs or tighten availability

regulatory.description: Removal of tax depreciation on commercial/industrial building structures (NZ Government policy change) has increased current tax expense and reduced after-tax cash returns
Auckland Unitary Plan and consenting processes can delay development timelines (e.g. Spedding Road subdivision, Harris Road redevelopment)

macro.risk: NZ economic weakness / tenant default risk
macro.description: A soft NZ economy, weak business confidence or rising unemployment could slow leasing demand, rent growth and increase tenant default/vacancy risk, particularly for SME tenants

Industrial property valuations are sensitive to movements in capitalisation rates; a reversal of the cap-rate compression trend (e.g. from renewed bond-yield increases) would drive fair-value losses through the income statement and reduce NTA per share, as seen in the FP24 stub period (fair value loss of ~NZ$90m)
Elevated build costs could compress development margins on the ~$325-350m committed/potential pipeline

execution.description: PFI changed its fiscal year end from 31 December to 30 June (effective FY2024/25), creating a six-month FP24 stub period that complicates historical comparability and CAGR analysis
Execution depends on PFI's small internal development team successfully delivering 11 planned projects on time and on budget without major cost overruns

macro_factors.industry_outlook: NZ industrial property, and Auckland industrial in particular, remains one of the more resilient commercial property sub-sectors. Auckland industrial vacancy was around 4.0% in H1 2026 (up ~30bps from 3.7%), with prime net rents up modestly (~1.5% in Q2 2026) and average net prime yields stable around 5.25% (secondary ~6.00%). Leasing demand was reported improving through late 2026 as vacancy is absorbed.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - industrial property is more defensive than office/retail due to structural logistics/e-commerce demand and land scarcity, but still sensitive to NZ GDP growth, business investment and interest rates via cap rates
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - both directly (variable-rate and hedge-roll-off debt costs) and indirectly (capitalisation rates used to value the ~NZ$2.25bn+ investment property portfolio, which drives reported profit via fair-value movements and NTA per share)

recent_developments.event: FY2026 full-year results (year to 30 June 2026): profit after tax of NZ$77.7m (down from NZ$106.0m in FY2025, reflecting a smaller fair-value gain of $16.1m vs $70.7m); FFO up 20.7% to 12.90 cps; AFFO up 14.0% to 10.93 cps; FY2026 cash dividends of 9.50 cps, up 10.5% on FY2025; gearing 34.2% (expected to rise to ~35.7% post committed acquisitions/development); occupancy 98.7%, WALT 5.04 years; portfolio ~7.1% under-rented; FY2027 dividend guidance of 9.75-9.85 cps

Issued NZ$200m PFI040 fixed rate bonds on the NZDX and progressed refinancing of syndicated bank facilities into a new ~$600m structure post balance date, diversifying and extending PFI's debt maturity profile

Announced divestment of non-core, out-of-Auckland properties: 2 Smart Road & 18 Constance Street, New Plymouth (NZ$4.70m) and 41 & 55 Foremans Road, Christchurch (NZ$14.35m), consistent with the strategy of recycling capital out of non-core holdings into Auckland development/acquisitions

H1 FY2026 (six months to 31 Dec 2025) result: profit after tax NZ$46.9m (up from NZ$28.8m pcp); AFFO 5.39 cps (up 23.9%); fair value gains of $17.1m (+3.2%) on 19 independently revalued properties; FY2026 dividend guidance raised to at least 9.05 cps (+5.2%); gearing stable at 34.2%; occupancy 99.9%, WALT 5.37 years; PFI020 $100m bonds repaid with bank facilities on maturity (1 Oct 2025)
Settled acquisition of 505-507 Mt Wellington Highway for NZ$36.0m, expanding the core Auckland industrial portfolio

Early lease surrender agreed with GrainCorp at 92-98 Harris Road, East Tamaki (surrender payment of NZ$5.12m recognised as rental income), accelerating access to a long-held brownfield redevelopment opportunity; demolition subsequently completed with the redevelopment now expected to be tenant-led

FY2025 (first full 12-month year under new 30 June balance date) results: profit after tax NZ$106.0m (vs a loss of $46.1m in the FP24 stub, driven by a $70.7m fair-value gain vs a $90.0m loss); FFO up 5.4% to 10.69 cps; AFFO up 8.1% to 9.59 cps; FY2025 cash dividends 8.60 cps; FY2026 dividend guidance (initial) of at least 8.90 cps; gearing 32.6%; portfolio value NZ$2.17bn; occupancy 99.9%, WALT 5.47 years; ~$700m of facilities refinanced/established including $150m PFI030 bonds (March 2025) at 5.43%; weighted average cost of debt fell to 4.52% from 5.72% following 250bp of OCR cuts since August 2024
Issued NZ$150m PFI030 fixed rate bonds on the NZDX at 5.43%, maturing September 2030

items.notes: Increase of ~2.6-3.7% on FY2026 dividends of 9.50 cps; implies a one-year AFFO payout ratio of ~95%, near/above the top of PFI's normal payout policy range
Up from 34.2% at FY2026 year-end as committed acquisitions and development capex are drawn; within the Group's 30-40% target range and well inside the <50% bank covenant

items.target: ~$325-350m over the medium term (excluding land already owned)
items.notes: 11 planned Green Star-rated development/redevelopment projects across Auckland industrial precincts (Springs Road, Harris Road, Spedding Road, Neilson Street, Patiki Road, Rosebank Road, Nesdale Avenue, Cryers Road); feasibility studies show development margins of ~15-20% versus low-to-mid 5% direct-acquisition cap rates

items.target: Portfolio ~7.1% under-rented as at Jun-2026 (narrowing from ~11.5% at Jun-2025)
items.notes: Expected to continue narrowing as rent reviews, renewals and market-rate leasing capture embedded reversion; FY2027 lease expiries were guided at ~7.8% of contract rent (excluding development opportunities)

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Simon Woodhams has characterised results through FY2025/H1 FY2026 as demonstrating 'the resilience of our industrial portfolio and the benefits of our long-term strategy,' citing sustained near-full occupancy, embedded under-renting as a multi-year growth lever, and a supportive falling-rate environment reducing the cost of debt. Management flagged that FY2026/FY2027 dividend guidance is subject to factors including leasing progress on the remaining speculative component of Springs Road Stage 2, clarity on Harris Road redevelopment plans/timing, and progress on material lease expiries.

bull_case: Structural Auckland industrial land scarcity supports near-full occupancy (98.7-99.9% across recent periods) and durable rental growth even as broader NZ commercial property cycles turn
Large embedded rent reversion (~7-11% under-rented across FY2025-FY2026) provides multi-year organic income growth largely independent of new leasing or acquisitions
Falling OCR/interest rates directly reduce PFI's cost of debt (down from 5.72% to ~4.5%) while supporting industrial cap rates and NTA per share
Self-funded, in-house $325-350m Green Star development pipeline captures 15-20% development margins versus mid-5% acquisition cap rates, an accretive use of capital unavailable to passive landlords

Internalised management structure, long-tenured board/leadership team (average tenure 6.7-8.6 years) and a 30+ year NZX track record (average ~9.3% total return since 1994 with dividends reinvested) support disciplined capital allocation
bear_case: Heavy Auckland concentration (~85-88% of portfolio) leaves PFI more exposed than diversified peers to any single-region downturn, oversupply or infrastructure shock
High dividend payout ratio (approaching or exceeding ~95% of AFFO in FY2026/FY2027 guidance) leaves minimal retained-earnings buffer, making growth reliant on continued debt/equity issuance

Reported profit is highly sensitive to non-cash fair-value movements on investment property; a reversal of recent cap-rate compression (as occurred in the FY2024 stub period, with a ~$90m fair-value loss) would hit both earnings and NTA per share

Rising gearing (34.2% moving toward ~35.7%, mid-range of 30-40% target) as development capex is drawn reduces balance sheet headroom just as speculative leasing risk (e.g. Springs Road Stage 2) remains unresolved
Valuation already reflects much of the reversion/development thesis - PFI trades at a premium P/E (~27x) to the global industrial REIT average (~17x), leaving limited margin for execution missteps
